title.es: Cómo empaquetan ideas los textos académicos

es: Reconocer cómo un verbo o un adjetivo se convierte en sustantivo (nominalización) para compactar información en un texto académico.

vocabulary.es: nominalización: convertir una acción o cualidad en sustantivo

teaching.en: Nominalisation turns actions into nouns, so cities grew rapidly becomes the rapid growth of cities, a compact noun phrase.
teaching.es: La nominalización convierte acciones en sustantivos, así que «las ciudades crecieron rápidamente» pasa a «el rápido crecimiento de las ciudades», un grupo nominal compacto.
teaching.explanationEs: El verbo grow pasa a growth, el adverbio rapidly pasa a adjetivo rapid y el sujeto original va detrás de of.
segments: Nominalisation turns actions into nouns, so cities grew rapidly becomes
the rapid growth of cities, a compact noun phrase.
teaching.audioText: Nominalisation turns actions into nouns, so cities grew rapidly becomes the rapid growth of cities, a compact noun phrase.

teaching.en: Dense prose often hides its actors: the adoption of the new method does not say who adopted it or why.
teaching.es: La prosa densa suele ocultar a sus protagonistas: «la adopción del nuevo método» no dice quién lo adoptó ni por qué.
teaching.explanationEs: Al nominalizar, el verbo adopt se convierte en una cosa y desaparece el sujeto que actuaba.
segments: Dense prose often hides its actors: the adoption of the
new method does not say who adopted it or why.
teaching.audioText: Dense prose often hides its actors: the adoption of the new method does not say who adopted it or why.

teaching.en: When a sentence seems impenetrable, unpack it: restore the verbs behind the nouns, and then say who did what to whom.
teaching.es: Cuando una frase parece impenetrable, desmenúzala: devuelve los verbos que hay detrás de los sustantivos y di quién hizo qué a quién.
teaching.explanationEs: Desnominalizar es el camino inverso: del sustantivo abstracto al verbo y a su sujeto.
segments: When a sentence seems impenetrable, unpack it: restore the verbs behind
the nouns, and then say who did what to whom.
teaching.audioText: When a sentence seems impenetrable, unpack it: restore the verbs behind the nouns, and then say who did what to whom.

teaching.en: Heightened awareness of the risk led to a significant reduction in accidents, and that nominalisation hides who became aware.
teaching.es: Una mayor sensibilización ante el riesgo llevó a una reducción considerable de los accidentes, y esa nominalización oculta quién se volvió consciente.
teaching.explanationEs: Aware pasa a awareness y reduce pasa a reduction: dos historias quedan comprimidas en una sola oración.
segments: Heightened awareness of the risk led to a significant reduction
in accidents, and that nominalisation hides who became aware.
teaching.audioText: Heightened awareness of the risk led to a significant reduction in accidents, and that nominalisation hides who became aware.

teaching.en: The efficiency of the service improved last year, where plainer writing would say that the service became more efficient.
teaching.es: La eficiencia del servicio mejoró el año pasado, donde una redacción más sencilla diría que el servicio se volvió más eficiente.
teaching.explanationEs: El adjetivo efficient pasa a efficiency (-ent a -ency); el grupo nominal entero es ahora el sujeto de improved.
segments: The efficiency of the service improved last year, where plainer
writing would say that the service became more efficient.
teaching.audioText: The efficiency of the service improved last year, where plainer writing would say that the service became more efficient.

teaching.en: A technical report may lend itself to nominalisation, but piling up nouns comes at the expense of clarity for any ordinary reader.
teaching.es: Un informe técnico puede prestarse a la nominalización, pero acumular sustantivos se hace a costa de la claridad para cualquier lector común.
teaching.explanationEs: Lend itself to significa «ser apropiado para»; at the expense of introduce lo que se sacrifica.
segments: A technical report may lend itself to nominalisation, but piling up
nouns comes at the expense of clarity for any ordinary reader.
teaching.audioText: A technical report may lend itself to nominalisation, but piling up nouns comes at the expense of clarity for any ordinary reader.

prompt.es: Elige la versión nominalizada de la oración del informe municipal.

choices.text: The adoption of the scheme by the council has led to the significant reduce of ring road accidents.
The council's adoption of the scheme has led to a significant reduction in accidents on the ring road.
The council's adopting of the scheme has significantly reduction in accidents on the ring road.

feedback.es: Adoption sustituye a adopted y reduction a fallen; el adverbio significantly pasa a adjetivo significant delante del sustantivo.

hint.es: Busca el sustantivo de adopt y el de reduce; el adverbio pasa a adjetivo.

origin.text: Since the council adopted the scheme last January, accidents on the ring road have fallen significantly, which has surprised even the engineers.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su cuidadosa evaluación de las pruebas convenció incluso a los escépticos.»

feedback.es: Assessment es el sustantivo de assess; aquí funciona como núcleo de un grupo nominal con of.

hint.es: Es el sustantivo de assess y termina en -ment.

origin.text: The committee studied the proposal for months. Its careful ___ of the evidence convinced even the critics.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El rápido crecimiento de la ciudad presionó a las escuelas locales.»

answer.text: The rapid growth of the city put pressure on local schools

feedback.es: El grupo nominal The rapid growth of the city es el sujeto y put pressure on es la parte verbal.

hint.es: Empieza por el grupo nominal que hace de sujeto.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada grupo nominal con la idea verbal que esconde.

pairs: the assessment of risk by trained experts
the efficiency of the new system

pairs.es: El nuevo sistema funciona con eficiencia
Los vecinos son ahora más conscientes

pairs: a significant reduction in waiting times

pairs.es: Los tiempos de espera se redujeron mucho

pairs: the rapid growth of the online market

pairs.es: El mercado en línea creció deprisa

feedback.es: Cada grupo nominal guarda un verbo o adjetivo: assess, efficient, aware, reduce y grow.

pairs: the assessment of risk by trained experts
the efficiency of the new system

pairs.es: El nuevo sistema funciona con eficiencia
Los vecinos son ahora más conscientes

pairs: a significant reduction in waiting times

pairs.es: Los tiempos de espera se redujeron mucho

pairs: the rapid growth of the online market

pairs.es: El mercado en línea creció deprisa

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué critica la investigadora de la expresión «the fall in confidence».

choices.text: It exaggerates the event by choosing a stronger word than the facts allow.
It makes a serious event sound milder than the figures suggest.
It condenses the event but leaves out who lost confidence and why.

feedback.es: La investigadora critica que el grupo nominal condensa el hecho y oculta quién perdió la confianza y por qué.

origin.audio: In her talk, the researcher describes the sudden fall in customer confidence after the announcement. That single noun phrase, she says, hides who lost confidence and why, which is exactly what makes dense prose so hard to question.

prompt.es: Completa: «Se menciona la adopción de una política, como si nadie la hubiera elegido.»

feedback.es: Adoption nominaliza el verbo adopt y deja a los responsables sin nombre, como sugiere el resto de la frase.

origin.text: The report never names the people in charge. It simply mentions the ___ of a new policy, as if nobody had chosen it.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere la autora sobre el estilo de este informe?

choices.text: That the style is so plain and repetitive that the figures cannot be trusted by careful readers.
That its easy style makes it hard to see who acted and how the figures were obtained.
That the committee left the figures out on purpose to protect itself.
That the complaints fell only because nobody was counting them any more.

feedback.es: La autora señala que el texto fluye pero no dice quién eligió ni cómo se contó: la prosa densa deja cifras sin personas responsables.

origin.text: The committee's conclusion rested on the rapid adoption of the new timetable and a marked reduction in complaints. Nowhere does the report say who chose the timetable, who complained, or how the complaints were counted. The paragraph reads easily, yet its dense prose leaves the reader with figures and no people to question about them.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la actitud de la conferenciante ante el titular.

choices.text: Dismissive: she regards the headline as false and wants it dropped.
Cautious: she wants the claims unpacked before she accepts them.
Curious: she wants to test the app herself and measure its effect on waste.

feedback.es: Ella no afirma que el titular sea falso, pero pide desmenuzar los grupos nominales antes de creerlo: postura cauta, no de rechazo ni de aplauso.

origin.audio: A lecturer is explaining why she doubts a headline. The headline said: rapid adoption of the app triggers a significant reduction in waste. She points out that the sentence is tidy and convincing, but that it conceals everything a careful reader needs to know. Who adopted the app, and how quickly? Waste of what, and measured by whom? She does not say the claim is false. Her point is that nominalisation lets a writer present a hopeful result as if it were simply a fact, so a reader must unpack the noun phrases before trusting the headline.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los artículos técnicos suelen prestarse a ellas.»

feedback.es: La colocación es lend itself to, «prestarse a»; con un sujeto plural (papers) el verbo queda en forma base: lend themselves to.

origin.text: Heavy noun phrases are not wrong in themselves. Technical papers often ___ themselves to them, but a leaflet for the public should stay closer to verbs.

prompt.es: Fusiona las dos ideas en una sola frase nominalizada, con un verbo de resultado.

answer.text: The improved efficiency of the service led to a significant reduction in complaints from customers.
accepted: The improved efficiency of the service led to a significant reduction in complaints from customers.
A greater efficiency of the service resulted in a reduction in the number of complaints.
The efficiency of the service brought about a reduction in complaints, which pleased customers.

feedback.es: Efficient pasa a efficiency y complain a complaints, y el verbo de resultado (led to) une las dos ideas.

origin.text: Ideas: el servicio se volvió más eficiente (efficient) y por eso los clientes se quejaron menos (complain). Escribe una sola frase que use efficiency y reduction.

evidenceGroups: reduction in the number of complaints

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la postura del autor ante la nominalización?

choices.text: Acceptable only in reports, and unsuitable for any other kind of text.
Wrongly attacked by critics, who should admire it as a sign of skill.
Cold and stiff in every case, although readers eventually get used to it.
Useful when used sparingly, but a nuisance when abstract nouns crowd together.

feedback.es: El autor defiende el recurso («lets a writer name an idea once») pero rechaza el amontonamiento de cinco sustantivos abstractos.

origin.text: Critics of formal style complain that nominalisation makes writing cold and stiff. I disagree, up to a point. A noun phrase such as the assessment of risk lets a writer name an idea once and then build on it. What I do object to is the crowd of abstract nouns: five of them in a single sentence is not skill, only extra work for the reader.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una reducción significativa de las quejas siguió al nuevo procedimiento.»

answer.text: A significant reduction in complaints followed the new method

feedback.es: El grupo nominal A significant reduction in complaints es el sujeto de followed.

prompt.es: Completa: «El resumen es muy breve, pero a costa de la claridad.»

feedback.es: At the expense of es la fórmula para lo que se sacrifica; at the cost of y at the price of son variantes posibles.

origin.text: The summary is very short, but it has been made so at the ___ of clarity, since none of the people involved are named.

es: Usar adjetivos evaluativos académicos (robust, flawed, compelling, tentative) para valorar un estudio con su razón, y reconocer la pasiva impersonal.

vocabulary.es: sólido, resistente (un resultado que se mantiene)
no alcanzar, quedarse corto respecto a

teaching.en: The results are robust: the sample was large, the method was clear, and the finding survived a second attempt.
teaching.es: Los resultados son sólidos: la muestra era grande, el método era claro y el hallazgo resistió un segundo intento.
teaching.explanationEs: Robust valora bien un resultado que se mantiene en distintas pruebas; la razón va tras los dos puntos.
segments: The results are robust: the sample was large, the method
was clear, and the finding survived a second attempt.
teaching.audioText: The results are robust: the sample was large, the method was clear, and the finding survived a second attempt.

teaching.en: A flawed design can cast doubt on every result that follows from it, however impressive the figures may look.
teaching.es: Un diseño con fallos puede sembrar dudas sobre todos los resultados que se derivan de él, por impresionantes que parezcan las cifras.
teaching.explanationEs: Cast doubt on es la colocación para debilitar la confianza en algo; however + adjetivo concede el atractivo de las cifras.
segments: A flawed design can cast doubt on every result that
follows from it, however impressive the figures may look.
teaching.audioText: A flawed design can cast doubt on every result that follows from it, however impressive the figures may look.

teaching.en: The evidence is compelling, since three independent teams found the same effect, and their combined data lend weight to the claim.
teaching.es: La evidencia es convincente, ya que tres equipos independientes hallaron el mismo efecto, y sus datos combinados dan peso a la afirmación.
teaching.explanationEs: Lend weight to significa «respaldar»; data se usa aquí como plural, por eso lend y no lends.
segments: The evidence is compelling, since three independent teams found the same
effect, and their combined data lend weight to the claim.
teaching.audioText: The evidence is compelling, since three independent teams found the same effect, and their combined data lend weight to the claim.

teaching.en: It is widely believed that coffee sharpens memory, but the authors stay tentative about one small study.
teaching.es: Se cree ampliamente que el café agudiza la memoria, pero los autores se muestran prudentes ante un solo estudio pequeño.
teaching.explanationEs: Repaso de la pasiva impersonal (it is believed that…) junto a tentative, que marca la cautela de los autores.
segments: It is widely believed that coffee sharpens memory, but
the authors stay tentative about one small study.
teaching.audioText: It is widely believed that coffee sharpens memory, but the authors stay tentative about one small study.

teaching.en: Even a thorough study can leave the proof far from conclusive if its methods fall short of accepted standards.
teaching.es: Incluso un estudio minucioso puede dejar la prueba lejos de ser concluyente si sus métodos no alcanzan los estándares aceptados.
teaching.explanationEs: Thorough elogia el cuidado; conclusive dice que la cuestión queda cerrada; fall short of = no llegar al nivel exigido.
segments: Even a thorough study can leave the proof far from
conclusive if its methods fall short of accepted standards.
teaching.audioText: Even a thorough study can leave the proof far from conclusive if its methods fall short of accepted standards.

teaching.en: Questionable wording may call into question an otherwise methodologically sound survey, because respondents can read the items differently.
teaching.es: Una redacción dudosa puede poner en entredicho una encuesta por lo demás metodológicamente correcta, porque los encuestados pueden leer las preguntas de otro modo.
teaching.explanationEs: Questionable es un adjetivo de cautela; call into question = poner en entredicho; otherwise = por lo demás.
segments: Questionable wording may call into question an otherwise methodologically
sound survey, because respondents can read the items differently.
teaching.audioText: Questionable wording may call into question an otherwise methodologically sound survey, because respondents can read the items differently.

prompt.es: Completa: «Por eso, el diseño del estudio tiene graves fallos.»

feedback.es: Flawed describe un diseño con fallos; la razón (muestra pequeña y elegida por amigos) está en la frase anterior.

hint.es: Adjetivo que señala un fallo de diseño y termina en -ed.

origin.text: Only twelve students took part, and all of them were chosen by the researcher's friends. For that reason, the design of the study is seriously ___.

prompt.es: Elige la valoración que combina el resultado y la actitud de los autores.

choices.text: The findings look flawed, since the authors call for further trials.
The findings look robust, so the authors sound conclusive.
The findings look robust, while the authors stay tentative.

feedback.es: El mismo patrón en seis países sugiere resultados sólidos, pero los autores escriben solo «may» y piden más ensayos: son prudentes.

hint.es: Un patrón repetido suena sólido; «may» y «further trials» suenan prudentes.

origin.text: A survey of five thousand adults in six countries found the same pattern each time. The authors, however, write only that it may indicate a link, and they call for further trials before drawing any firm conclusion.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Una muestra tan pequeña siembra dudas sobre todo el estudio.»

answer.text: Such a small sample casts doubt on the whole study

feedback.es: Such a + adjetivo + sustantivo pone el énfasis en el tamaño; casts doubt on sigue a un sujeto singular.

hint.es: Such a va antes del adjetivo y del sustantivo.

prompt.es: Elige el adjetivo que evalúa con precisión cada estudio.

feedback.es: Cada razón apunta a un adjetivo: muestra sesgada, flawed; efecto que resiste cada repetición, robust; argumento al que cuesta oponerse, compelling; primer vistazo, tentative.

sentences: Only ten people took part and the sample was biased, so the design is ___.
The same effect survived every repetition of the test and in every country, so the result is ___.
Three independent teams reached the same view and a careful reader would struggle to disagree, so the case is ___.
The authors call it a first look and ask for more trials, so their conclusion is ___.
origin.text: Four studies reached the college reading group this week. Evaluate each one with the adjective that fits its evidence best: robust, flawed, compelling or tentative.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la hablante del estudio.

choices.text: The method impressed her, but the wording of the survey makes her hesitate.
The method impressed her, but the survey wording leads her to reject the paper completely.
The survey wording worried her, but the method made her fully trust the result anyway.

feedback.es: Elogia el método (thorough), pero duda de las preguntas (questionable) y por eso aplaza su confianza: no rechaza el estudio ni lo acepta sin reservas.

origin.audio: I read the whole paper this morning. The method is thorough, since every step is checked and explained. But the survey questions are questionable, so I would not trust the headline result just yet. I would call the conclusions tentative at best.

prompt.es: ¿Qué valoración del experimento es la más precisa?

choices.text: Flawed: a single trial with volunteers can never show anything.
Tentative: a small first trial that hints at a possible benefit.
Conclusive: a small result that already settles the question.

feedback.es: El equipo realizó el experimento una sola vez, con treinta voluntarios, y pide un ensayo mayor: es un resultado provisional, no concluyente.

origin.text: The team ran the experiment once, with thirty volunteers, and reported a small improvement. They write that the data are consistent with a benefit, but that a larger trial is needed before any firm conclusion can be drawn.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la evaluadora sobre la afirmación principal del estudio?

choices.text: That the statistics are weak and should be repeated by another independent team of researchers.
That the tea obviously has no effect, since the teacher caused the result.
That a comparison group would prove the authors' claim completely.
That careful work does not justify so firm a claim from such limited evidence.

feedback.es: La evaluadora elogia el trabajo, pero señala que una sola aula sin grupo de comparación no basta para una afirmación tan firme.

origin.text: Reviewer's report: The authors have plainly worked hard. Their survey is thorough, and their statistics are handled with care. Yet the headline claim, that green tea improves concentration, rests on a single classroom in one school, with no comparison group. One is left wondering whether the tea, the teacher or the time of day made the difference.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué quiere enseñar la profesora sobre cómo valorar un estudio pequeño.

choices.text: That a judgement is fair only when the claim is no bigger than the evidence.
That a small sample is an acceptable reason to call any study flawed.
That honest authors should avoid tentative language to sound more convincing.
That a study should be evaluated by the size of its sample and nothing else.

feedback.es: La profesora dice que un estudio pequeño puede ser honesto si sus afirmaciones son prudentes; el fallo está en la distancia entre evidencia y afirmación.

origin.audio: When you evaluate a study, do not reach for the strongest word. Calling a study flawed because its sample is small is fair only if the authors claim more than that sample allows. A small study that says tentative things can be perfectly honest. Suppose two teams each test forty people. One team writes that the medicine always works; the other writes that the result is encouraging and deserves a larger trial. Their data may be the same, and yet only the first team has gone too far. The real fault is a claim that is bigger than its evidence.

prompt.es: Completa: «El segundo informe no alcanzó el nivel exigido.»

feedback.es: Fall short of es la colocación para «no alcanzar» un nivel o estándar.

origin.text: The committee read all three reports with care. The second, however, fell ___ of the standard required, because it gave no details of how the participants were chosen.

prompt.es: Valora el estudio en dos frases: resultado, razón y actitud de los autores.

answer.text: The results are robust and the method is thorough, since three thousand people in five countries showed the same pattern. Even so, the authors remain tentative and call for more trials before any firm conclusion is drawn.
accepted: The results are robust and the method is thorough, since three thousand people in five countries showed the same pattern. Even so, the authors remain tentative and call for more trials before any firm conclusion is drawn.
The findings are robust, because people in five countries produced the same result every time. The authors are tentative, however, and ask for further trials before any firm conclusion is drawn.
The evidence is compelling, since 3000 people in five countries gave the same result. Nevertheless, the authors remain cautious and call for more trials.

feedback.es: Un buen comentario combina un adjetivo preciso, la razón con datos del estudio y la cautela de los autores.

origin.text: Datos: 3000 participantes de cinco países; el mismo resultado en cada réplica del experimento; método revisado paso a paso. Los autores escriben que sus conclusiones son provisionales y piden más ensayos.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe el autor este párrafo?

choices.text: To warn readers that late meals are dangerous for their sleep and their general health.
To show that a popular idea is not the same as a proven one.
To argue that thirty trials are too few to decide anything.
To defend late meals against unfair reviews of the evidence.

feedback.es: El autor no dice que cenar tarde sea bueno ni malo: señala que una idea puede ser popular y reconfortante sin estar respaldada por pruebas.

origin.text: It is widely believed that eating late at night ruins sleep, and advice columns repeat it every winter. Yet a review that pooled thirty trials found no clear effect. The reviewers do not say that late meals are good for you; they say the evidence is simply not there. A claim can be popular, old and comforting without ever becoming well supported.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Los datos no son concluyentes, pero el estudio es minucioso.»

answer.text: The data are not conclusive, yet the study is thorough
accepted: The data are not conclusive, yet the study is thorough
The study is thorough, yet the data are not conclusive

feedback.es: Yet introduce el contraste: lo minucioso del estudio no basta para que los datos sean concluyentes.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula evaluativa con su sentido.

feedback.es: Las cuatro fórmulas sirven para valorar: respaldar, poner en entredicho, no alcanzar y sembrar dudas.

title.es: Leer un resumen de estudio a toda velocidad

es: Leer un abstract y extraer objetivo, método, resultado y postura del autor, distinguiendo una inferencia justificada de una exagerada.

vocabulary.es: datos declarados por los propios participantes

teaching.en: The opening of an abstract states its aim: what the authors set out to examine, and why the question matters.
teaching.es: El comienzo de un abstract enuncia su objetivo: lo que los autores se propusieron examinar y por qué importa la pregunta.
teaching.explanationEs: Aim va seguido de to + verbo o de una oración con whether; se narra en pasado.
segments: The opening of an abstract states its aim: what the
authors set out to examine, and why the question matters.
teaching.audioText: The opening of an abstract states its aim: what the authors set out to examine, and why the question matters.

teaching.en: The method tells you who took part and for how long: we followed 240 adolescents in four schools for one year.
teaching.es: El método dice quién participó y durante cuánto tiempo: seguimos a 240 adolescentes en cuatro colegios durante un año.
teaching.explanationEs: Fíjate en los números y en la duración: sirven para juzgar si el estudio es lo bastante grande.
segments: The method tells you who took part and for how long:
we followed 240 adolescents in four schools for one year.
teaching.audioText: The method tells you who took part and for how long: we followed 240 adolescents in four schools for one year.

teaching.en: Self-reported data, such as sleep diaries, are useful but open to error, because adolescents may remember their nights inaccurately.
teaching.es: Los datos declarados por los propios participantes, como los diarios de sueño, son útiles pero admiten errores, porque los adolescentes pueden recordar mal sus noches.
teaching.explanationEs: Self-reported avisa de que la medición depende de lo que dicen los participantes, no de un instrumento.
segments: Self-reported data, such as sleep diaries, are useful but open
to error, because adolescents may remember their nights inaccurately.
teaching.audioText: Self-reported data, such as sleep diaries, are useful but open to error, because adolescents may remember their nights inaccurately.

teaching.en: These findings point to a benefit for adolescents, yet the authors avoid a causal link because the design cannot rule out other explanations.
teaching.es: Estos hallazgos apuntan a un beneficio para los adolescentes, pero los autores evitan un vínculo causal porque el diseño no puede descartar otras explicaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Point to es más cauto que prove; rule out significa descartar; una correlación no es una causa.
segments: These findings point to a benefit for adolescents, yet the authors avoid
a causal link because the design cannot rule out other explanations.
teaching.audioText: These findings point to a benefit for adolescents, yet the authors avoid a causal link because the design cannot rule out other explanations.

teaching.en: You may draw an inference only if it stays in line with the data; anything bolder needs further research.
teaching.es: Solo puedes sacar una inferencia si se mantiene en consonancia con los datos; algo más atrevido requiere más investigación.
teaching.explanationEs: Una inferencia justificada no va más allá de lo que dicen los datos; further research señala el límite.
segments: You may draw an inference only if it stays in
line with the data; anything bolder needs further research.
teaching.audioText: You may draw an inference only if it stays in line with the data; anything bolder needs further research.

teaching.en: A hedged claim uses may, suggest or tend to, and this stance tells you how cautious the authors are about the benefit.
teaching.es: Una afirmación matizada usa may, suggest o tend to, y esta postura indica lo cautos que son los autores sobre el beneficio.
teaching.explanationEs: Hedge significa atenuar una afirmación; los verbos modales y de cita revelan la postura.
segments: A hedged claim uses may, suggest or tend to, and this
stance tells you how cautious the authors are about the benefit.
teaching.audioText: A hedged claim uses may, suggest or tend to, and this stance tells you how cautious the authors are about the benefit.

prompt.es: ¿En qué campo del abstract aparece esta frase y qué información aporta?

choices.text: Method: it tells us who took part and how long the study lasted.
Aim: it tells us why the authors chose this question and what they hoped to find.
Conclusion: it tells us how far the authors are willing to go.

feedback.es: Es el método: dice cuántos estudiantes, en cuántos colegios y durante cuánto tiempo; no plantea la pregunta ni extrae conclusiones.

hint.es: Fíjate en las cifras y en la duración.

origin.text: We followed 240 adolescents in four schools for one year; two schools moved the start of the day to nine o'clock, and two did not.

prompt.es: Completa: «El objetivo de este estudio era examinar si el ruido afecta a la memoria.»

feedback.es: Aim introduce la pregunta del estudio y va seguido de to + verbo.

hint.es: Sustantivo de tres letras que significa objetivo.

origin.text: Researchers often open an abstract with a sentence of purpose. The ___ of this study was to examine whether background noise affects adolescents' memory.

sentences: Aim: to examine whether phone use in lessons ___ exam results.

origin.text: Aim: This study examined whether phone use in lessons lowers exam results among adolescents. Method: We tracked 600 students in twelve schools for two terms; half of the schools banned phones in class. Results: Students in schools with a ban scored about four per cent higher, but the difference narrowed in the second term. Conclusion: The findings point to a small benefit, although we cannot rule out other explanations, and further research is needed.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo presentan los autores su resultado.

choices.text: As a small improvement that they see as important because it appeared in a final test.
As a small improvement that they treat with care because of how it was measured.
As a small improvement that they put down to the fact that it lasted only six weeks.

feedback.es: Los autores hablan de una diferencia pequeña y de datos declarados por los propios participantes, y piden más ensayos: prudencia, no entusiasmo.

origin.audio: This study asked whether language apps help adults learn vocabulary. We tested two hundred adults for six weeks. Those who used the app remembered more words in a final test, but the difference was small, and most of the data were self-reported. We therefore describe the effect as small and call for further trials.

prompt.es: ¿Qué inferencia está justificada por estos resultados?

choices.text: Anyone who sleeps nine hours instead of six will score higher on memory tests.
The five-point gain proves that longer sleep is what causes better memory.
Longer sleep may help memory, although volunteers may not speak for all teenagers.

feedback.es: La conclusión usa may y reconoce que los participantes eran voluntarios; las otras dos frases generalizan o afirman una causa sin apoyo en los datos.

origin.text: Results: Teenagers who slept nine hours scored five points higher on a memory test than those who slept six. Conclusion: Longer sleep may improve memory in adolescents, although all the participants were volunteers.

prompt.es: ¿Qué inferencia va más allá de lo que sostiene el abstract?

choices.text: Every school in every country will see better attention if lessons start later.
Later starts may help adolescents sleep longer, at least in this city.
The attention results rest partly on what students said about themselves.

feedback.es: El abstract solo apunta a un posible beneficio en cuatro colegios de una ciudad; extenderlo a todos los colegios del mundo es una exageración.

origin.text: Aim: This study examined whether later school start times improve the sleep and attention of adolescents. Method: We followed 240 students in four schools for one year; two schools moved the start of the day to nine o'clock, and two did not. Results: At the later schools, students slept about fifty minutes longer each night and reported better attention, although attention was self-reported. Conclusion: These findings point to a possible benefit. Because all four schools were in one city, we cannot rule out local factors, and further research is needed.

choices.text: Confident: the data prove the idea, but they ask for further trials anyway.

feedback.es: Dicen que los datos están «in line with» la idea, «nothing more»: postura prudente, ni de prueba ni de rechazo.

origin.audio: Our sample was small, sixty runners, and all of them were club members. Those who slept longer reported fewer injuries. We do not claim that sleep prevents injury. answer.text: According to the council's study, the building of more than a hundred kilometres of new lanes for cyclists has been followed by a sharp growth in commuter cycling, from 3 to 11 per cent, and by a reduction in central traffic of nine per cent. Early opposition, especially from shopkeepers who feared losing customers to reduced parking, has proved wrong. The lead researcher argues that the scheme has already earned back its cost, since spending on road maintenance and health care has dropped, and she notes that shops beside the lanes now earn six per cent more. Some critics claim, however, that the findings for small firms cannot be trusted, because just forty of them replied. The researcher concedes that this is a weakness and recommends a second, larger survey next year, while the council, for its part, is considering further routes outside the centre but has not explained where the money will come from.
accepted: According to the council's study, the building of more than a hundred kilometres of new lanes for cyclists has been followed by a sharp growth in commuter cycling, from 3 to 11 per cent, and by a reduction in central traffic of nine per cent. The lead researcher argues that the scheme has already earned back its cost, since spending on road maintenance and health care has dropped, and she notes that shops beside the lanes now earn six per cent more. Some critics claim, however, that the findings for small firms cannot be trusted, because just forty of them replied. The researcher concedes that this is a weakness and recommends a second, larger survey next year, while the council, for its part, is considering further routes outside the centre but has not explained where the money will come from.

Since the council built its protected bike lanes, the published figures point to a rise in cycling to work and a fall in traffic, together with cleaner air. The lead researcher maintains that the project has already repaid its cost, noting lower spending on roads and health care and higher sales in shops beside the lanes. Some critics claim that the evidence on small businesses is unreliable, since few of them replied. She acknowledges that weakness and recommends a second, larger survey next year, while the council is already looking at further routes for cyclists.

Five years on, the study reports a growth in cycling and a decrease in central traffic, together with cleaner air and quieter streets. The lead researcher contends that the project has paid back its cost, because road repairs and health care now cost less, and she adds that shops beside the lanes are selling more. Critics claim that the findings on small shops cannot be trusted, since only forty of them replied. She admits this limit and suggests repeating the survey after a year with a wider sample, while the council is looking at further routes outside the centre.

feedback.es: Una buena paráfrasis cambia la estructura, atribuye cada idea una sola vez con verbos distintos, condensa con nominalizaciones y no copia frases del original.

origin.text: Five years ago, the city council decided to build more than one hundred kilometres of protected bike lanes. At first, many residents opposed the plan, and shop owners were especially worried, because they assumed that fewer parking places would mean fewer customers. However, the figures published this spring tell a different story. The proportion of people who cycle to work has risen from three per cent to eleven per cent, while car traffic in the centre has fallen by nine per cent. Air quality has improved, the main streets are quieter, and several schools report that more pupils now arrive by bicycle. The researcher who led the study argues that the investment has already paid for itself, because the city now spends less on road repairs and on health care. She points out that sales in the shops along the new lanes have grown by six per cent. Nevertheless, some critics claim that the results for small shops are unreliable, since only forty businesses answered the survey. The researcher acknowledges this limitation, and she suggests that the council should repeat the survey next year with a larger sample. Meanwhile, the council hopes to build more lanes in the north of the city, although it has not yet said who will pay for them.

origin.text: The council argues that the lanes are a success, but its figures come from its own survey, and it has not published the questions. Nobody outside the council can tell whether residents were asked fairly. It may be a good survey; it may not. Until the council shows its method, the claim rests on trust.

choices.text: Not yet: the result is promising but cannot safely be extended to everyone.
Yes, in general: the findings match earlier work, so the result can be extended.
No: the pilot study was too small to show anything at all about exercise.

feedback.es: El ponente dice «Not quite»: el resultado es prometedor y coincide con trabajos previos, pero con voluntarios es difícil generalizar y faltan los mayores; tampoco descarta el efecto.

origin.audio: Someone asked me whether exercise improves memory for everyone. Not quite. The study followed sixty adults, all of them volunteers, and the improvement was about eight per cent. It is thought that exercise helps, and the findings are in line with earlier work, but it is difficult to generalise from volunteers. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, with the proviso that older adults were not tested. I should add that this was a pilot study with a small sample, so it is thought that a larger trial would give a clearer picture, but nobody can say for certain until it is carried out.

origin.text: The improvement is thought to be small, and part of it may be ___ to the fact that all the participants were eager volunteers.

prompt.es: Resume el estudio: objetivo, método, resultado, pasiva impersonal y respuesta.

answer.text: The aim of this study was to examine whether taking notes by hand helps students remember more than typing. Briefly, one hundred and twenty students were followed for three weeks, and half of them wrote their notes by hand. Overall, the students who wrote by hand recalled six per cent more in a final test. It is widely assumed that handwriting is better for memory, and these findings are in line with that idea. It is worth noting that part of the difference may be attributed to motivation, since those students were all volunteers. To answer your question, we cannot say that handwriting is better for everyone, because all the participants came from one college, and it is difficult to generalise from a single group. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, and further research with students of different ages is needed before anyone gives firm advice to students.

This study asked whether taking notes by hand is better for memory than typing them. Briefly, a hundred and twenty students took part for three weeks, and half of them wrote by hand. Overall, the handwriters remembered six per cent more in the final test. It is often believed that writing by hand helps memory, and the results are in line with that view. However, everybody came from the same college, so we cannot say that handwriting is better for all students; it is difficult to generalise from one school. It is worth noting that some of the difference could be attributed to motivation. The conclusion is tentative, and further research is needed.

The aim was to examine whether students who write their notes by hand remember more than students who type. Briefly, one hundred and twenty students were tested over three weeks, and half of them used pens. Overall, the handwriters recalled six per cent more. It is thought that handwriting slows people down and helps them think, which is in line with these findings. To answer your question, it is difficult to generalise, since every participant belonged to one college, and we cannot say that the method works for everyone. On balance, the conclusion is tentative, with the proviso that more research is needed with different groups of students.

feedback.es: Un resumen completo recorre objetivo, método, resultado y límite, usa una pasiva impersonal y responde a la duda con prudencia.

origin.text: Estudio: ¿tomar apuntes a mano ayuda a recordar más que escribirlos en el teclado? 120 estudiantes durante tres semanas; la mitad escribió a mano. Los que escribieron a mano recordaron un 6 % más en una prueba final. Todos venían de un mismo colegio. Un compañero pregunta: «¿Podemos decir que escribir a mano es mejor para la memoria?» Escribe el resumen, usa una pasiva impersonal y responde con cautela.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito escribe la autora «I would not generalise beyond first-year students»?

choices.text: To limit her answer to the kind of students that the study actually examined.
To say that first-year students are the only ones who should revise in this way.
To refuse to answer her classmate's question about the paper.
To warn that the paper is unreliable because it is old.

feedback.es: Delimita su respuesta a los estudiantes del estudio: es la prudencia de quien no extiende el resultado más allá de la muestra.

origin.text: Dear group, here is the summary you asked for. The aim was to compare two methods of revision. It has been shown that testing yourself beats reading your notes again, but the effect is thought to be smaller for difficult topics. I would not generalise from first-year students to students in later years. I hope that answers your question, and I am happy to share the paper.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se cree ampliamente que el efecto es pequeño.»

answer.text: It is widely believed that the effect is small

feedback.es: It is widely believed that + oración es la pasiva impersonal con un adverbio de grado; it es obligatorio.
